steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: How far is County Hillock?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Far.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: My sister must have known...

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Only The Elocutionist and his band of idiots would consider this plan flawless.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Then why are you still following me?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Oh, believe me, if it were up to me I'd be taking a nap in camp right about now.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Why didn't my sister stop me?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: I don't know. Maybe she has high hopes for you.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: No, that's impossible. She's never looked at me like that. When I agreed to be her shadow, she...

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Please, Harmonie... tell her I don't want to do this.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: That you don't want to go to County Hillock?

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Mhm. And if she's in a good mood, could you also tell her that, from now on, I'll—

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: No, never mind.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Fine, can't hurt to pass it along, I suppose. Although it's not easy avoiding The Elocutionist's eyes and ears.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Thank you. You should go...

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: ...before she gets bored.

a.text: Harmonie did not return until after they arrived at County Hillock. She knew what that meant.
That night, when cannons roared and crystals bloomed, she lay on the streets of County Hillock, blood draining from her abdomen.
She had not been afraid then. Instead, she felt relieved that she would die like any other person.
But then she saw those purple flames, on a tower not too far away.
That was when she felt afraid.
Afraid that the flames would overlook her and turn her into another puppet like those on the street.
Afraid that the flames would find her and bring her back, forcing her to remain a shadow.
She gazed into the fire, trying to find some hint of her future in it, but saw nothing but apathy.
That which she feared most had finally happened.

steps.text: The dead dragon lies on the ground.
Behind the living dragon, the wayward wakewoman suddenly understands it all.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: She deceived you.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: No, she didn't deceive anyone.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: She set this all up, knowing you would never allow the entire city to die with her!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: She baited you into piercing her vessel, freeing her from her bonds and allowing the purple fire to spread, burning us all to ashes on the eve of Samhain!

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Why would she take such a risk for a festival that she never cared about?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'm affected by the purple flames too. I can feel the flames of death burning in my chest, colder than ever. So cold I'm growing number by the minute!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: It doesn't matter whether she's seeking dominion over all of Tara, or if she's simply gone mad and wants the city to die with her!

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: It's neither. Tara already belongs to her, and she was very much lucid. She...

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: She—

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Nemos, is her body still there?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'll go check.
The wayward wakewoman's brow is furrowed. Perhaps she has never felt such malice in all her life, and as such has never harbored such resolve.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Her body is—
The sound of burning drowns out her answer.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Whatever she's trying to do, Na Saoirsí is not fully gone. The fire-returning ceremony can still go on... it must go on.

spans.text: Whatever she's trying to do, Na Saoirsí is not fully gone. The fire-returning ceremony can still go on... it

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'm well aware.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'll inform the citizens that the wicked red dragon they worshipped is dead.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: What about Brigid?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I've asked her to leave the city and find the wakemen.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: And how are you going to tell people that Eblana is dead?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: With a coffin. That seems appropriate.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Even coffins are in short supply, but she is not some nameless nobody. She deserves one.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Is something wrong?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: No. I'm simply realizing how ugly the path she walked is, a path that even now waves at me invitingly... And it's an invitation I have no choice but to accept.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Go, Nemos. I will buy you some time.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: You mean from the dark mist?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Yes. If it wants to be a part of the Samhain festivities, I will keep it at bay.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I can hardly wait to ask the mist how to return the Red Dragon's flame to darkness.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: 'I can hardly wait to ask the mist how to return the Red Dragon's flame to darkness.'

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: How do you feel about that line?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Now, the ending of the dragon and her reflection is clear enough.
The writer stands up with a start.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Who are you and what do you want?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: All I want is to finish the story that you would not.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Didn't you say I was the type who liked to piece together the truth? We've gotten so very close to it.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: This is enough. I'm leaving—

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: If you won't tell the ending yourself, I suppose it falls on me.

a.text: Suddenly, someone opened their eyes, causing a surprised reflection to let go of her hand. The dragon fell into the fire burning bright, and the reflection hid back in the mirror.
When the fire subsided, the dragon was gone, and the people were anxious, for they could not find their dragon.
The reflection wanted to explain, find a way to bring the dragon back. Without the dragon, though, she could no longer leave the mirror.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: You've been glancing over there at the newspapers. But not everything reported is a fact.
The writer looks towards the door.
He tries to imagine himself running out of the tavern, but it is such a preposterous proposition that he almost laughs out loud.
If not everything reported is a fact, then he finally knows who this woman is, and why she is here.
He also knows that there is no escape.
But there is something else he realizes.
Perhaps this is his chance to truly find the ending he had hoped for.
No matter who she is, as long as the story continues, they are equals.
He feels his spirit return.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Okay. I don't care who you are, or why you're here, but that's no way to tell a story.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: You haven't given it an ending. All you did was extend an ending-less story.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: But I have to know—did you... really see a red dragon kill another?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: In the same sense that you saw the hero drag a giant metal skeleton to the square. A creative liberty, nothing more.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Then take responsibility for it. So the dragon in the mirror accidentally caused her other self to burn to death in the fire. What next? What did the people do? What about the dragon in the mirror?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: What about you? Don't you have any ideas of your own?

For the first time in a long while, the writer takes out a fountain pen from his pocket, then grabs one of the playing cards on the table. He tries to write something, but the tip of the pen has dried out from disuse.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: I need... time.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: But if it can be connected... then maybe...

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Connected?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Let me guess. You're talking about the last story that you published?
The writer's pen scratches hard against the card. Finally, some ink oozes out of the tip.
He is suddenly reminded of the words of Seamus Williams—'May death connect us with all legends.'
Seamus Williams is dead. But he himself might—if he may be so impertinent—have a chance to be connected with the legends he wrote.
He tries to scribble the poem on the card, but the pen leaves only broken, illegible ink trails.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Just maybe...

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Yes?
The writer sits back on the chair, his back even straighter than before.
He suddenly feels an urge, the same one he felt after hearing a Seamus Williams poem for the first time.
The same feeling that had taken him down this wretched path, which seizes his chest and makes him want to sing, to yell—
To create.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: You may have indeed solved a problem for me.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: As I said, what I've seen, what I believe, and what I've said all contradict one another. Thanks to you, though, they are finally beginning to converge.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: How lovely for you.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Now, are you ready to start telling the third story?

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Of course... of course.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: But I'll need your help.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: You will need to pick up the narrative whenever I get stuck.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: This is my story, but it's also yours.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: It has always been yours.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: With pleasure.
The writer's breathing is rapid, his face red. His fountain pen still refuses to write, so he throws it on the table.
Yes. Of course.
Has he not seen enough of those things already?
So what?
He is a writer. He will soon find the ending of his story.
